headline: Nestlé's chief executive says workers need to understand what AI can do and how it could change their company, not just how to write good prompts.
score_reason: Lowered from 4: Business Insider published the interview on 8 Oct 2026, before the window, and it is general advice from one chief executive.
importance_line: Office workers are told what a chief executive expects of them as AI spreads, which carries weight because Nestlé announced plans to cut about 16,000 jobs partly through automation (The Next Web), but this is general advice from one executive and the interview describes no specific Nestlé plan.
summary: Business Insider reports, in an interview published on 8 Oct 2026, that Nestlé chief executive Philipp Navratil, who leads the food and drinks maker behind Nespresso and DiGiorno with more than 270,000 employees, says knowing how to write good prompts is not enough, and that workers must also understand their business and what AI can do and where it is heading, though not its technical workings. He warns that adding AI on top of existing habits can make work more complicated, and wants staff to rethink their processes and drop unneeded steps so time is freed for analysing data and meeting business partners.
notes: The pool item is Livemint's 11 Oct 2026 rewrite of this Business Insider interview, so the original was read and is the source and url. The interview is dated 8 Oct 2026, before the window. The 16,000 job-cut figure in the importance line comes from The Next Web (8 Oct 2026), not from Business Insider.
